analysis.subject: physics
analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers the Wright 1903 engine with four cylinders and four-stroke operation, mechanical steps from Stage 3 compression to Stage 4 combustion at nearly constant volume, and thermodynamics showing temperature and pressure increase with heat release.

overview.headline: Wright engine four-stroke combustion raises temperature and pressure at constant volume

keyPoints.point: The Wright engine consisted of four cylinders with pistons connected to a common crankshaft to produce thrust.
keyPoints.quote: four cylinders like the one shown above, with each piston connected to a common crankshaft which turns the propellers to produce thrust.

keyPoints.point: A four-stroke engine completes four movements of the piston before the firing sequence is repeated.
keyPoints.quote: there are four movements (strokes) of the piston before the entire engine firing sequence is repeated.

keyPoints.point: Combustion proceeds so quickly that the piston is considered motionless and volume of the combustion chamber stays constant.
keyPoints.quote: The combustion proceeds so quickly that we can consider the piston to be motionless and the volume of the combustion chamber to be a constant.

keyPoints.point: Temperature and pressure in the combustion chamber both increase during the combustion process as heat is released.
keyPoints.quote: Temperature and pressure in the combustion chamber both increase during the combustion process.

keyTerms.gloss: enclosed chamber where volume stays constant while combustion raises temperature
keyTerms.quote: the volume of the combustion chamber to be a constant.

keyTerms.gloss: engine type where four piston movements complete one firing sequence
keyTerms.quote: called a four-stroke engine because there are four movements (strokes) of the piston

keyTerms.gloss: common shaft connected to pistons that turns to produce thrust for propellers
keyTerms.quote: with each piston connected to a common crankshaft which turns the propellers to produce thrust.

keyTerms.gloss: engine cycle that designates conditions as Stage 3 and Stage 4
keyTerms.quote: we designate this condition as Stage 3 of the Otto cycle.

keyTerms.gloss: heat capacity at constant volume that controls temperature rise for a given heat release
keyTerms.quote: and cv is the specific heat at constant volume, and T is the temperature.

keyTerms.gloss: gases produced by combustion whose temperature increases in the chamber
keyTerms.quote: The combustion increases the temperature of the exhaust gases, any residual air in the combustion chamber, and the combustion chamber itself.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Sequence shows mechanical stages from compression through spark and combustion to power stroke in taught order.
componentPlan.focusQuote: The end of the combustion process is designated Stage 4 of the engine cycle and is the beginning of the power stroke.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Explorer lets students vary heat release and specific heat to see temperature rise at constant volume.
